column1: # CHAOS-3141 deterministic package weights for Go integration CI sharding.
# The first data row declares the shard count. Remaining rows are
# <repository-relative package key><TAB><estimated seconds>. The package set is
# checked against ci/check_go.sh's live integration-tag discovery before any
# shard runs, so this file cannot silently omit or duplicate a package.
# Most weights are rounded up from the latest complete go-storage-integration
# runner (2026-08-03) or PR #1733's completed package lines (2026-08-11).
# internal/providersync is rounded from the exact current-feature local run,
# 1165.894s. internal/streamhandlers is ceil() of its own local run,
# 112.639s (CHAOS-4194): almost all of that is ClickHouse container startup --
# six tests, each taking a fresh container so the real migration chain is
# applied to a clean database rather than to whatever an earlier test left
# behind -- so the weight scales with the TEST COUNT in that file, not with the
# assertions in them. Re-time it if that file grows. Longest-processing-time-first assignment keeps the two
# non-dominant shards balanced while isolating that indivisible dominant
# package under the unchanged 25-minute job budget.
# internal/jobs/workgraph/edges (CHAOS-4766): ONE test, which takes a fresh
# ClickHouse container and then applies the real migration chain via
# chschema.Apply. Weighted by the header's own rule for container-dominated
# packages -- scale with test count, not assertion count. 20s is ceil() of
# internal/streamhandlers' per-test cost (113s / 8 tests = 14.1s, same
# container-plus-migrations shape) plus margin, because a single test amortises
# nothing. This is an ESTIMATE, not a measurement: re-time it from a completed
# go-storage-integration runner and correct it, and re-time it if the file
# gains tests.
# internal/platform/config (CHAOS-5560): two tests, each taking a fresh
# container -- one PostgreSQL, one ClickHouse -- to prove a DSN assembled
# from discrete components reaches the real server with reserved characters
# intact. Container-dominated, so the header's rule applies: scale with test
# count, not assertions. 30s is the local wall time of two consecutive
# `go test -count=1 -tags=integration` runs (15.89s, 15.42s) rounded up with
# margin for a slower hosted runner. This is an ESTIMATE, not a CI
# measurement: re-time it from a completed go-storage-integration runner and
# correct it, and re-time it if that file gains tests.
# cmd/query-api/internal/analytics (CHAOS-4730): un-denylisted (CHAOS-4643's
# reason no longer held once the package got real Testcontainers coverage,
# see ci/check_go.sh's INTEGRATION_DENYLIST comment). Weight 22s, ceil() of a
# local run of both its Testcontainers-backed tests together (21.575s,
# breakdown_seeded_integration_test.go + investmentquality_seeded_integration_test.go,
# each starting its own container).
# cmd/query-api/internal/investmentexplain (CHAOS-4977 step 7): TWO
# Testcontainers-backed tests in workunitreader_seeded_integration_test.go,
# each taking a fresh ClickHouse container plus a small DDL/seed chain --
# the recurrence guards for the step-7 live-differential findings that (1)
# FetchWorkUnitInvestments could not scan the real Map(String, Float64)
# theme/subcategory columns, and (2) FetchWorkUnitInvestmentQuotes could
# not bind a pair list against the real driver at all (added after the
# first test; same file, same container-per-test shape). Weight 41s,
# ceil() of 2x internal/jobs/workgraph/edges' own single-test estimate
# above (+1s margin) -- same container-plus-migrations shape, weight
# scales with TEST COUNT per the header's own rule (this is an ESTIMATE,
# not a measurement -- re-time from a completed go-storage-integration
# runner and correct it, and re-time again if the file gains more tests).
# internal/jobs/investment/chquery (CHAOS-4441): weight 122s, ceil() of a local
# run of all seven of its Testcontainers-backed tests together (121.469s). Same
# shape as internal/streamhandlers above -- almost all of that is ClickHouse
# container startup plus the real migration chain, applied to a clean database
# per test rather than to whatever an earlier test left behind, so the weight
# scales with the TEST COUNT in that file, not with the assertions in them.
# Re-time it if that file grows.
# internal/jobs/investment/chwrite (CHAOS-4441): weight 130s. MEASURED on
# bigboy (arm64 compute host, no local Docker available for this lane) --
# `go test -tags=integration -count=1 ./internal/jobs/investment/chwrite/...`,
# all five Testcontainers-backed tests, each starting its own ClickHouse
# container: 128.101s package time. Rounded up to 130 for headroom, same
# reasoning as internal/storage/postgres/authschema below -- the weight is
# only used for shard BALANCING, so a little over-statement costs packing
# efficiency while under-stating risks a shard blowing its job budget. This
# venue (bigboy) runs roughly 2x local wall-clock (see the bigboy lane
# recipe's timing table), so this number is a conservative UPPER bound, not
# a CI-equivalent measurement -- re-time it if a faster reference becomes
# available, and re-time regardless if tests are added (weight scales with
# TEST COUNT here, same as its chquery sibling above).
# internal/storage/postgres/authschema (CHAOS-4882): weight 60s. MEASURED, not
# estimated -- a local run of all 15 Testcontainers-backed tests together took
# 23.467s package time, each starting its own PostgreSQL container. (The
# reachability test's fourth SUBTEST does not add a container: subtests share
# their parent's fixture, which is why the weight tracks top-level test count
# rather than assertion count.)
# (Two earlier revisions of this note said 2.752s for two tests and 11.404s for
# four. Each was re-measured rather than left describing a run that no longer
# existed: the note below says to re-time when tests are added, and a stale
# derivation standing beside a number nobody re-derived is the exact defect
# this ticket's review rounds kept finding.) PostgreSQL starts far faster than the
# ClickHouse-backed packages above, which is why this is still an order of
# magnitude cheaper than internal/streamhandlers.
# Rounded UP to 30 for CI headroom: the local run had a warm image, and the
# weight is only used for shard BALANCING, so over-stating a cheap package
# costs a little packing efficiency while under-stating one can push a shard
# past the 25-minute job budget. The weight SCALES WITH TEST COUNT here, since
# almost all of it is container startup -- re-time it if tests are added.
# internal/testsupport/chschema (CHAOS-4902): weight 75s. MEASURED on bigboy
# (arm64 compute host, no local Docker available for this lane) -- `go test
# -tags=integration -count=1 ./internal/testsupport/chschema/...`, both
# Testcontainers-backed tests sharing one ClickHouse container plus the real
# migration chain applied via chschema.Apply: 72.615s package time. Rounded
# up to 75 for headroom, same reasoning as every other entry in this file --
# the weight is only used for shard BALANCING, so a little over-statement
# costs packing efficiency while under-stating risks a shard blowing its job
# budget. Bigboy runs roughly 2x local wall-clock (see the bigboy lane
# recipe's timing table), so this is a conservative UPPER bound, not a
# CI-equivalent measurement -- re-time it if a faster reference becomes
# available, and re-time regardless if tests are added.
# internal/teamownership (CHAOS-4897): weight 45s. Codex review round 2
# (2026-09-04, P3) caught this entry going stale ONE COMMIT after it was
# written (bumped 20s -> 30s for a second test); round 3's P1 fix (the
# owned-repo query now also resolves GitHub provider_access rows, repo_id
# NULL, by joining `repos` on name) added a THIRD Testcontainers-backed
# test, TestOwnedRepoIDsResolvesProviderAccessRowsByRepoName, same
# container-plus-migration shape as internal/jobs/workgraph/edges above.
# Re-MEASURED on bigboy (arm64 compute host) with all three tests: `go test
# -tags=integration -count=1 ./internal/teamownership/...`: 13.62s +
# 13.57s + 13.77s = 40.96s package time. Rounded up to 45 for headroom,
# same reasoning as every other entry in this file -- the weight is only
# used for shard BALANCING. Bigboy runs roughly 2x local wall-clock (see
# the bigboy lane recipe's timing table), so this is a conservative UPPER
# bound, not a CI-equivalent measurement --
# re-time it if a faster reference becomes available, and re-time
# regardless if tests are added (weight scales with TEST COUNT here, same
# as its container-plus-migration siblings above).
# internal/jobs/workgraph/operationaledges (CHAOS-4924): FIVE
# Testcontainers-backed tests in incidents_golden_integration_test.go, each
# taking a fresh ClickHouse container plus the real migration chain -- same
# container-plus-migration shape as internal/jobs/workgraph/edges above,
# weight scales with TEST COUNT per the header's own rule. Measured
# DIRECTLY on bigboy (not a local run needing the 2x scale-up other entries
# apply): `go test -tags=integration -coverprofile=... ./internal/jobs/workgraph/operationaledges/...`,
# the five tests). Rounded up to 65 for headroom, same reasoning as every
# other entry in this file -- re-time if a faster reference becomes
# available, and re-time regardless if the file gains more tests.
# internal/jobs/operational (CHAOS-5318/CHAOS-5319): 19 tests total, ALL
# Testcontainers-backed (5 github_app_events_integration_test.go + 14
# sync_dispatch_integration_test.go), each taking a fresh Postgres container
# -- same container-per-test shape as internal/jobs/workgraph/edges above,
# weight scales with TEST COUNT per the header's own rule. Re-timed on
# CHAOS-5319 r1's corrective commit (2026-09-06, sync_dispatch_integration_
# test.go grew from 9 to 14 tests -- the parent-planner-managed-config
# resolution path, its own five new cases). Measured DIRECTLY on bigboy (not
# a local run needing the 2x scale-up other entries apply):
# `go test -tags=integration -count=1 ./internal/jobs/operational/...`,
# 48.755s package time. Rounded up to 55 for headroom, same reasoning as
# every other entry in this file -- re-time if a faster reference becomes
# available, and re-time regardless if either integration test file gains
# more tests.
# cmd/query-api (CHAOS-5349): weight raised 15 -> 110. The package gained
# capacity_forecast_seeded_integration_test.go, FOUR Testcontainers-backed
# tests that each take a fresh ClickHouse container AND apply the real
# migration chain via chschema.Apply -- the same container-plus-migrations
# shape as internal/testsupport/chschema and internal/jobs/workgraph/edges
# above, so the weight scales with TEST COUNT, not with assertions.
# MEASURED DIRECTLY on bigboy (arm64 compute host, not a local run needing
# the 2x scale-up other entries apply):
# `go test -tags=integration -count=1 -run TestCapacityForecast ./cmd/query-api/`
# reported 106.763s package time for the four new tests. Rounded up to 110
# for headroom, and the pre-existing route/readyz integration tests in this
# package are inside that number since the run compiled and linked the whole
# package. Re-time it if this file gains tests.

# cmd/go-api-routing (CHAOS-5486, 2026-09-10): this package's FIRST
# -tags=integration file, verbs_integration_test.go. It exists because an
# adversarial round showed that four mutations at REAL call sites in this
# package -- the DSN-leaking flag default restored inside runEnable, the
# schema-agreement preflight disabled, the enabled_unproven WARNING
# suppressed, and an ORDER BY tiebreak dropped -- all survived the whole
# suite at 53.2% command coverage, because nothing ever ran a verb end to
# end. Two of the four need a real database to kill.
# NINE Testcontainers-backed tests as of r2's fix round (up from two):
# each takes a fresh Postgres container so the real FK and the mode CHECK
# are exercised against a clean database. r2 added seven -- a held-lock
# `status` deadline test, the two preflight-3 halves (not-registered,
# digest-divergent), enable's -expect-build cross-check, a two-operation
# unproven-warning test, a UTF-8 sibling-sweep unit test (no container),
# and repoint's OWN -expect-build cross-check (the pairwise-knob sweep's
# own finding: enable's had an end-to-end killer, repoint's did not) --
# closing six mutants (M20-M23, M80) plus the repoint expect-build gap
# that the original two tests' single-operation, no-concurrency shape
# could not reach. MEASURED on bigboy 2026-09-10, whole package,
# -count=1, twice: 38.673s and 35.637s. Rounded up to 45 for CI headroom,
# the same treatment the other per-test-container packages in this file
# get. Re-time if it gains tests.
# r4 fix round (2026-09-11): ONE more Testcontainers-backed test added
# (TestStatusReportsDeployedDocumentDigestMismatchNotHealthy, killing M27 --
# `status` discarding the deployed registry's per-operation document
# digest). Re-measured, whole package, -count=1: 31.975s. Still comfortably
# inside the existing 45 weight; not raised.
# opus r6 fix round (2026-09-11): TEN more Testcontainers-backed tests
# added across F1-F5/T1/observability (a deterministic deadlock repro,
# an empty-registry write-verb refusal pair, a dead-rows guard test, a
# stale-digest refusal, a classification-vs-database-error separation, a
# genuine server-side-failure exit-code test, and an endpoint/per-row-log
# test, among others). Re-measured, whole package, -count=1, twice:
# 57.222s and 54.166s. Raised 45 -> 70 for CI headroom.
# opus r7 fix round (2026-09-11): THREE more Testcontainers-backed tests
# added (F1's all-registered/stale-only skip test, F4's before-state
# value-naming test, and T1 M38/M40's combined live-row-plus-stale-digest
# disable test), plus several plain-suite-only fixes (F2/F3/F5/F6/F7/F8)
# that add no container. Re-measured, whole package, -count=1, twice:
# 73.754s and 75.610s -- over the 70 ceiling both times. Raised 70 -> 90
# for CI headroom.
# opus r9 fix round (2026-09-11): ONE more Testcontainers-backed test
# added (enable -dry-run's row-count invariance, killing the mutant that
# silently applied a dry run). Re-measured, whole package, -count=1,
# three times under concurrent host load: 79.329s, 88.456s, 92.720s --
# over the 90 ceiling on the third run. Raised 90 -> 110 for CI headroom.

# deterministic concurrency tests (each holds a blocking transaction open until

# Measured on bigboy 2026-09-09, -count=1: 101.96s, then 113.98s, then 111.12s.
# The step numbers match the ones recorded beside the shard-balance assertion
# in tests/tooling/test_go_integration_sharding.py, deliberately: two records
# of one history that disagree are worse than one.
# RE-MEASURED 2026-09-10 on the rebase onto 8a0590b22, whole package,
# -count=1, twice: 108.80s and 109.70s. LOWER than the 113.98s the 120
# was rounded from, even though this rebase ADDS one integration test
# (the canary/primary re-point killer) -- container startup is the
# variance and this host was quieter. 120 is left where it is rather than
# lowered: it is an upper bound with headroom, the measurement still sits
# under it, and moving a weight down to chase a quiet run is how a
# manifest starts under-booking CI. The shard-balance assertion in
# tests/tooling/test_go_integration_sharding.py was re-run against the 54
# packages main now discovers (CHAOS-5523 and CHAOS-4806 each added one)
# and shards 2/3 land at 933s/934s -- still within 1s.
# THAT AGREEMENT WAS BROKEN ONCE, BY REBASING, AND NOTHING CAUGHT IT. Four
# successive rebases resolved this file by taking the newer side wholesale --
# right for the WEIGHT, wrong for the COMMENT -- so the number advanced while
# its justification reverted, and the file spent several hours recording 120
# under prose explaining 90. ci/check_go.sh sums the numbers and never reads
# the prose, so no test could have failed. If you resolve a conflict here,
# read the result rather than the diff.
# RAISED 120 -> 135, r2's fix round (2026-09-10): one new test

# bigboy 2026-09-10, whole package, -count=1: 130.89s -- above the 120

# up to 135 for the same shard-balance headroom the prior raises used.
# RAISED 135 -> 155, r3's fix round (2026-09-11): no new integration
# test added to this package this round (the case-shadow/UTF-8 killers
# for r3's findings are plain-suite unit tests, no container). Re-measured
# anyway per Trap #105 discipline, whole package, -count=1: 141.43s --
# still fits under 135 by nothing meaningful, and this host was running
# 3+ other lanes' Go suites concurrently at measurement time (unlike the
# 130.89s baseline, which was closer to isolated). Rounded up to 155 for
# real headroom rather than re-asserting a ceiling already this close to
# the last clean measurement.
# RAISED 155 -> 175, same r3 round, second re-measurement (team-lead's
# decoder-sweep follow-up: LoadDocuments converted off its last struct-tag
# decode, still no new integration test in this package): -count=1 came
# back at 157.80s, over 155 by a small amount -- the same concurrent-
# host-load story as the 141.43s measurement above, not a package
# regression, but two consecutive over-ceiling reads on a host this busy
# means the number is being chased instead of given real headroom.
# Rounded up to 175 to stop re-measuring this weight every round.
# CHAOS-5505, rebased onto the 175 tip above (not the 120 this branch
# started from): the audit-row writes add ten more container-per-test
# tests, and every routing verb's existing test now also builds
# go_api_routing_audits so its write meets the real CHECK constraints.
# First measured pre-rebase on bigboy 2026-09-09, -count=1: 126.50s on a

# concurrent on the same host at the time (6% CPU utilisation for the
# whole run) -- not a usable number. 175 was kept as PR #2448's tip
# rather than ratcheted off a loaded local run.
# CORRECTED per this file's own stated plan: PR #2448's first hosted CI

# 2 job 103446098966 -- `ok github.com/full-chaos/dev-health-ops/internal/goapiproof
# 234.482s`. This is the first REAL measurement since the 175 ceiling was
# set from noisy local runs; corrected 175 -> 235 (ceil + headroom, same
# rounding convention as every raise above).
# CHAOS-5507, stacked on the corrected 235: the lock-order guard adds
